st: What COVID and climate change taught us about cities

sec.p: It's a fact: we increasingly live in urbanised, “non-rural” areas, which many nations define as settlements of 2,000-10,000 people. As a percentage of the population:

sec.t: ff.34.2 Rethinking cities: mobility and traffic
sec.p: Even if most Italians live outside settlements of 1M people, they often travel to these nerve centres for work during the day. And we know it well, given the amount of traffic (especially between Pero and Cormano). COVID and remote working have improved things a bit. But how…
Speaking of Amsterdam and the Netherlands. In the '70s the Dutch were staunch supporters of cars and turned 900-year-old canals into roads.
With last summer's heatwaves (don't you miss it a bit, apart from the Jova Beach Party?), we realised it's better not to hold the Ferragosto barbecue in the city.
Finally, let's get philosophical, fortissimo, right?
